action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Limb NCS shows whether the facial diplegia is part of a generalised polyradiculoneuropathy, which separates the GBS variant from bilateral Bell's palsy and other cranial neuropathies; facial and blink studies document the facial nerve involvement [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports GBS and excludes the lymphocytic meningitis of Lyme neuroborreliosis, neurosarcoidosis, HIV and basal infective or malignant meningitis, the main causes of facial diplegia [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No brainstem lesion, mass or leptomeningeal enhancement; facial nerve enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI with gadolinium and thin sections through the facial nerves
action_criteria.rationale: Bilateral facial palsy calls for imaging to exclude a pontine lesion, a skull-base or parotid mass and leptomeningeal disease before it is attributed to a polyradiculoneuropathy.

action_criteria.label: Lyme serology
action_criteria.rationale: Lyme neuroborreliosis is a leading cause of bilateral facial palsy and is treatable; serology is part of the facial diplegia work-up.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-GQ1b IgG negative, with full eye movements and no ataxia: no Miller Fisher overlap
action_criteria.label: Optional serum anti-GQ1b IgG for a Miller Fisher overlap
action_criteria.rationale: Anti-ganglioside antibodies are not needed for the bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant; anti-GQ1b is advised only when Miller Fisher syndrome or an overlap is suspected (EAN/PNS 2023), which full eye movements and normal gait make unlikely here.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics and give the baseline before any immunotherapy [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: The variant can progress to limb, bulbar and respiratory weakness within days; serial FVC, MIP and MEP (with a face mask when lip seal is poor) set the level of monitoring [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: normal sinus rhythm 64-92 bpm and blood pressure 114/70 to 132/82 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction can occur in any GBS variant and cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while the disease progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm with normal PR, QRS and QTc intervals as the baseline
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic rhythm and conduction changes [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.label: Optional chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy (sarcoidosis)
action_criteria.rationale: Sarcoidosis is a cause of facial diplegia; chest imaging looks for hilar lymphadenopathy, but the acellular CSF and the polyradiculoneuropathy already make it unlikely.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No current medications, so no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check before IVIg or plasma exchange (no current medications)
action_criteria.rationale: He takes no medicines, so the check cannot change management (ROUND_POLICY ruling 6).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on the variant and on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on the bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored bed with serial FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours (face mask, since lip seal is poor) and a bedside swallow and cough assessment before oral intake; move to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 60% predicted or 20 mL/kg (about 1.5 L at 76 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -40 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, FVC falls by more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough or pooled secretions develops [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

IVIg or plasma exchange is not routinely advised while he walks unaided and the weakness stays confined to the face; start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange if he loses the ability to walk unaided or develops bulbar, respiratory or autonomic involvement [EAN_PNS_2023].
Protect both corneas: lubricating drops by day and ointment with lid taping or a moisture chamber at night for bilateral lagophthalmos.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while the disease progresses.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant

differential.key_features: A leading cause of facial diplegia, but there is no tick bite, rash or travel, Lyme serology is negative and the CSF has 2 cells/mm3 (neuroborreliosis gives a lymphocytic pleocytosis).

Facial nerve is the cranial nerve most often involved, but there are no systemic features, serum ACE is normal, the CSF is acellular and MRI shows no leptomeningeal enhancement (chest CT, if done, shows no hilar lymphadenopathy).
A diagnosis of exclusion; distal paresthesias, generalised hyporeflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation and demyelinating limb NCS show a polyradiculoneuropathy.

differential.diagnosis: Miller Fisher syndrome or GBS overlap
differential.key_features: Full eye movements, no ataxia, no limb weakness and anti-GQ1b negative.
No headache or fever, CSF acellular with normal glucose and negative Gram stain, AFB smear, cryptococcal antigen and culture, and no meningeal enhancement on MRI.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
No ptosis, ophthalmoparesis or fatigability; areflexia, paresthesias, CSF dissociation and demyelinating NCS are not features of MG.

key_clinical_evidence: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness with distal paresthesias, reduced reflexes and no limb weakness is the bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant of GBS [Wakerley_2014]; the Brighton certainty levels do not apply without limb weakness.

CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 78 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and demyelinating limb nerve conduction with sural sparing show a polyradiculoneuropathy beyond the facial nerves, which bilateral Bell's palsy does not produce and which argues against Lyme neuroborreliosis and neurosarcoidosis, both of which usually raise the CSF cell count.
Bilateral facial palsy is rarely idiopathic: Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, HIV, basal meningeal processes and brainstem lesions are excluded with serology, CSF and MRI.
Anti-ganglioside antibodies are not needed to diagnose typical GBS; anti-GQ1b is tested when Miller Fisher syndrome or an overlap is suspected [EAN_PNS_2023].
He walks and runs (GBS disability score 1), so IVIg is not routinely advised; he is admitted and monitored because the variant can progress to limb, bulbar or respiratory weakness [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Sequential bilateral facial palsy within two days, preceded by distal paresthesias and accompanied by generalised hyporeflexia, is a polyradiculoneuropathy until proven otherwise; the CSF and NCS confirm it.
red_herrings.data_point: Primary care diagnosis of right Bell's palsy two days ago
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors on idiopathic facial palsy, so the second side is read as bilateral Bell's palsy

general.query: bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant of Guillain-Barre syndrome

results.finding: Bifacial weakness with paresthesias is a localised GBS variant: facial diplegia, distal paresthesias and reduced reflexes without limb weakness; it is distinguished from facial diplegia due to Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, HIV and basal meningeal processes.

IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided; in mildly affected patients treatment is not routinely advised within 2 weeks of onset unless they progress; corticosteroids are not advised.

general.summary: Bifacial weakness with paresthesias is a recognised localised GBS variant; there is no trial evidence for immunotherapy in localised variants, and the guideline indication for IVIg or plasma exchange is inability to walk unaided or progression [Wakerley_2014, EAN_PNS_2023].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Bilateral facial motor neuropathy: prolonged distal latencies and low CMAP amplitudes, with absent R1 and R2 blink responses in an efferent pattern. 2. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in median and peroneal nerves. 3. Prolonged median and absent peroneal F-waves; absent H-reflexes. 4. Reduced median with normal sural sensory amplitudes. 5. Reduced recruitment in facial muscles; normal limb needle EMG. Findings are consistent with a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with bilateral facial nerve involvement. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.pattern: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with bilateral facial nerve involvement

metadata.difficulty_description: Bilateral facial palsy with distal paresthesias and hyporeflexia but no limb weakness: the bifacial weakness with paresthesias variant of GBS, after exclusion of Lyme disease, sarcoidosis and intracranial causes.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry) plus brain MRI and Lyme serology to exclude the mimics of facial diplegia; 1 red herring (the initial Bell's palsy diagnosis).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Two days of progressive weakness of both sides of the face, with drooling and inability to close the eyes; tingling in the fingers and feet for six days.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. H. is a 36-year-old IT specialist. Six days ago he noticed tingling in the tips of his fingers and in both feet, which has persisted without spreading. Two days ago the right side of his face became weak; his primary care physician diagnosed a right Bell's palsy. Yesterday the left side became weak as well, and this morning he awoke unable to close either eye, with drooping of both cheeks, inability to purse his lips and drooling of saliva. He cannot frown, show his teeth, blow or whistle. He has lost taste bilaterally and his speech is slurred because he cannot move his lips. He has no limb weakness, difficulty walking, double vision, unsteadiness, swallowing difficulty or shortness of breath. There is no earache, hearing change, tinnitus, rash, headache, neck stiffness, photophobia or fever, and no bladder or bowel symptoms. He reports no recent infection, travel, tick or insect bites, or trauma. He has never had a similar episode.

neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose and heel-shin testing normal. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral complete lower motor neuron facial weakness: unable to close either eye, bilateral lagophthalmos with Bell's phenomenon preserved; unable to frown, show teeth, blow or whistle; nasolabial folds absent bilaterally; drooling. Taste reduced bilaterally on the anterior tongue. Labial dysarthria. Jaw closure strong; facial sensation intact. No ptosis. Pupils equal and reactive. Full extraocular movements without diplopia or fatigable weakness. Palate elevates symmetrically; gag present; tongue and neck flexion strength normal.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal gait; walks on heels and toes and can run.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone. Power 5/5 in all muscle groups of the upper and lower limbs, including neck flexion and extension.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Ankle jerks absent bilaterally; knee, biceps, triceps and brachioradialis reflexes 1+ and symmetric. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Distal tingling in the fingers and toes. Vibration sense mildly reduced at the great toes (6 s at the halluces), normal at the ankles and fingers. Pinprick, temperature and joint position sense intact. No sensory level.

physical_exam.general: Weight 76 kg, height 175 cm. No rash, lymphadenopathy, parotid swelling or uveitis.
